name: Tajikistan-Afghanistan border attacks
started: 2025-08-24 (escalating clashes; attacks on Chinese workers from Nov 2025)
summary: The Tajik-Afghan frontier along the Panj river has become a small but deadly flashpoint, with five Chinese mining and construction workers killed in cross-border attacks in late November 2025 and repeated firefights between Tajik border guards and infiltrators. China told its citizens to leave the border area.

sides.name: Tajikistan
backers: CSTO (border equipment programme approved 10 Dec 2025; Russia, Belarus and Kazakhstan to supply)
China (reportedly may be assisting with border policing)
sides.strength: About 80 border outposts built in the past two to three years (Wikipedia).

sides.name: Armed groups and Taliban forces on the Afghan side
members: Armed groups based in Afghanistan (blamed by Tajik authorities as criminal groups)
Taliban border forces (clashes in Aug and Oct 2025)
Jamaat Ansarullah (set up an 'Ansar' unit near the border in Kunduz)

background: Tajikistan has been openly critical of the Taliban government, which in turn has warned Dushanbe against interfering in Afghan affairs, and their border with Afghanistan is long, mountainous and porous. Chinese companies operate gold mines and infrastructure projects on the Tajik bank, including in Shamsiddin Shohin district, and disputes over mining and shifts in the river's course have sparked clashes with Taliban forces. This matters because attacks on Chinese nationals draw Beijing into Central Asian security and test the Taliban's promises to stop militants using Afghan soil.
year: Clashes with Taliban fighters near Shamsiddin Shohin on 24 August and 26 October 2025 were followed by talks. On 26 November 2025 a drone strike from Afghan territory killed three Chinese nationals on the Tajik side, and on 30 November fire from Ruzvayak village in Badakhshan's Mohi Mai district killed two more; Tajikistan blamed Afghan-based criminal groups and demanded Taliban action. The CSTO approved border equipment on 10 December, President Rahmon opened four new outposts on 24 December, and on 25 December an infiltration into Khatlon left three militants and two Tajik border guards dead. Tajik guards killed four infiltrators on 19 January 2026 and three of five armed men in Shamsiddin Shohin on 30 January 2026. The source counted 17 armed clashes on the border in 2025.
situation: As of the latest sourced information (January 2026), Tajik forces were engaging infiltrators every few weeks; no sourced incidents after January 2026 were found for this research.
technical: 26 Nov 2025: drone-delivered attack on the Tajik side killed 3 Chinese nationals and wounded 1 (Wikipedia).
30 Nov 2025: cross-border fire from Ruzvayak, Mohi Mai district, Badakhshan killed 2 Chinese nationals and wounded 2 (Wikipedia).
24 Aug 2025: heavy weapons reportedly used in a Taliban-Tajik clash in Dovang District, Badakhshan, near Shamsiddin Shohin; one Taliban fighter killed (Wikipedia).
CSTO five-year border programme (approved 2024) entered equipment-delivery phase on 10 Dec 2025 (Wikipedia).
Tajikistan has built about 80 border outposts in two to three years; four new outposts and a tank training ground opened 24 Dec 2025 (Wikipedia).
Jamaat Ansarullah set up an 'Ansar' unit in Imam Sahib District, Kunduz, near the Tajik border (Feb 2025) (Wikipedia).
casualties: 5 Chinese nationals killed (Nov 2025); 2 Tajik border guards killed (25 Dec 2025); at least 10 militants killed in Dec 2025 to Jan 2026 clashes (Wikipedia).

timeline.event: Drone strike kills three Chinese nationals on the Tajik side.
Cross-border fire kills two more Chinese nationals.
CSTO approves military equipment for Tajik border.
Infiltration into Khatlon foiled; 3 militants and 2 border guards killed.
Tajik border guards kill four militants in Khatlon.
Clash in Shamsiddin Shohin; three armed men killed.

outlook: Watch for further attacks on Chinese projects, Chinese security involvement in Tajikistan, and whether Taliban-Tajik talks over mining and river-course disputes hold.

zones.name: Shamsiddin Shohin district (Khatlon)
zones.note: Chinese gold-mining area; drone attack on Chinese workers and Jan 2026 clash (approximate).

zones.name: Darvoz and Badakhshan border
zones.note: Mountain frontier opposite Afghan Badakhshan, incl. Mohi Mai district (approximate).

zones.name: Khatlon lowland border (Panj river)
zones.note: Infiltration routes; Dec 2025 and Jan 2026 clashes (approximate).

battles.name: Khatlon border infiltration clash
battles.outcome: Infiltration foiled; Tajikistan criticised the Taliban and demanded an apology.
battles.losses: 3 militants and 2 Tajik border guards killed (Wikipedia).
battles.significance: The deadliest clash for Tajik forces in the window, followed by further fatal clashes in January 2026.

battles.name: Cross-border attacks on Chinese workers in Tajikistan
battles.place: Shamsiddin Shohin district, Khatlon, Tajikistan (approximate location)
sides: Chinese workers in Tajikistan / Tajik Border Troops
battles.outcome: Two attacks from Afghan territory, the first by drone, the second by gunfire from Ruzvayak village in Mohi Mai district, Badakhshan; China urged its citizens to leave the border area.
battles.forces: Drone with explosives (26 Nov); small-arms fire across the river (30 Nov).
battles.significance: The first deadly attacks on Chinese workers from Taliban-ruled Afghanistan, testing Beijing's relationship with Kabul and drawing the CSTO into strengthening the border.
